html:
The Nawa are a Panoan people of the upper Juruá River in Acre, western Brazil, near the Serra do Divisor on the Peruvian border.

During the rubber boom of around 1900 rubber bosses attacked and enslaved them, and for most of the 1900s they were thought to have died out. In the late 1990s families in the area began to claim Nawa identity again, and they have since sought recognition of their land. Related Panoan peoples include the Yaminawá, the Huni Kuin and the Shanenawa.
